findings.title: enableSqlExpressions ignores the feature flag and always returns false
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false in both branches of the following `if`. The flag value is discarded, so the function is dead logic that reads as if it honours the flag. Anyone later restoring a flag-based gate will find an inverted-looking expression that never reaches a true result. It also dereferences `h.features` on every SQL query, so a nil feature set would panic on the SQL path, which previously never touched features. A plain rejection with a comment explaining the disablement would be clearer.

findings.title: No regression test asserts that SQL expression queries are rejected
findings.body: This is a security hotfix for RCE/LFI, but the PR adds no test showing that ReadQuery returns an error for QueryTypeSQL regardless of feature flags, and none that NewSQLCommand or UnmarshalSQLCommand fail for arbitrary SQL. Without such a test, a future change could silently re-enable the path (for example by restoring the DuckDB implementation in pkg/expr/sql/db.go) and nothing would catch it.

findings.title: Existing SQL parsing and execution tests will fail, and no test files were updated
findings.body: TablesList now always errors because DB.RunCommands is a stub returning "not implemented", and NewSQLCommand and SQLCommand.Execute depend on it. The PR changes no test files. If the repository's existing tests for TablesList, NewSQLCommand, SQL command execution, or the reader's SQL path (pkg/expr/sql, pkg/expr, reader tests) expect DuckDB results, they will fail in CI. Those tests should be removed, skipped with an explanation, or converted to assert the disabled behaviour.

findings.title: Error message says 'not implemented' for a deliberate disablement
findings.body: When a user enables the sqlExpressions flag, every SQL query now fails with "sqlExpressions is not implemented". That is misleading: the feature is disabled by policy after a security fix, not missing. Users and support will read it as a bug. The feature toggle and its docs still describe SQL expressions as enabled by the flag, which the PR explicitly leaves untouched. The message and the flag documentation should say the feature is disabled for security reasons.

findings.title: DuckDB-era string-built SQL is left in place; the fix depends entirely on the stub
findings.body: TablesList still builds a SQL command with fmt.Sprintf and only escapes single quotes before sending it to the engine. The security property now relies entirely on the stub DB in db.go returning errors. Nothing in the reader or parser enforces the gate if the real engine is restored. Anyone who reinstates the DuckDB backend would reintroduce the injection surface without any warning in the code path. Either remove the dead parser code or add a comment and a guard tying its use to the feature gate.

findings.title: Stub DB named like a working in-memory engine with no doc comment
findings.body: NewInMemoryDB and the DB type suggest a functional in-memory SQL engine, but every method unconditionally returns "not implemented". The type has no doc comment saying it is an intentional fail-closed stub that disables SQL expressions. A maintainer reading only this file could mistake the failures for a bug, or reinstate a DuckDB backend without knowing the stub is the security boundary.

findings.title: Checksum removals unrelated to go-duck are unexplained
findings.body: The go.work.sum hunk removes checksum lines for github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/storage/azblob v1.3.2 and github.com/google/go-replayers/grpcreplay and httpreplay. These are not part of the go-duck removal, and nothing in the PR explains them. This looks like side effects of a tidy run on a different module graph. Removing needed checksums can cause 'missing go.sum entry' failures in builds that run with -mod=readonly. Reviewers should confirm these modules are not needed, or drop the unrelated churn.
